SYNTHETIC VISIT SUMMARY. Fictional patient, for interview use only. Not medical advice.

Patient: Alex R., 30, male
Visit type: Virtual video visit
Reason for visit: Known mild asthma. More wheezing and coughing at night for 5 days after a cold. Speaking in full sentences, no distress during the visit.

Assessment: Mild asthma flare triggered by a viral infection.

Plan:
- Salbutamol (blue reliever puffer) 100 mcg: 2 puffs with a spacer every 4 to 6 hours as needed for wheeze or shortness of breath.
- Start fluticasone 125 mcg (controller puffer): 1 puff twice daily, every day, even when feeling well. Rinse your mouth after each use.
- Follow up with your family doctor in 2 to 4 weeks.

When to seek care:
- Needing the blue puffer more often than every 4 hours: book a visit the same day.
- The blue puffer is not helping, you cannot speak in full sentences, or your lips or fingernails look blue or grey: call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department.

SYNTHETIC VISIT SUMMARY. Fictional patient, for interview use only. Not medical advice.

Patient: Maya T., 4 years old, female, weight 16 kg (visit attended by parent)
Visit type: Virtual video visit, with an otoscope image taken at a partner pharmacy
Reason for visit: Left ear pain and fever (38.5°C) since yesterday. Eating and drinking normally.

Assessment: Left middle ear infection (acute otitis media).

Plan:
- Amoxicillin suspension 400 mg/5 mL: give 9 mL by mouth twice daily for 5 days.
- Shake well before each dose and keep in the fridge.
- Children's acetaminophen (Tylenol) may be given for pain or fever, dosed by weight as directed on the package.
- Fever and ear pain usually improve within 48 to 72 hours of starting the antibiotic.

When to seek care:
- Fever still present after 48 to 72 hours on the antibiotic, or swelling or redness behind the ear: seek in-person care the same day.
- Stiff neck, unusual drowsiness or difficulty waking, or signs of dehydration: go to the nearest emergency department.

Patient: Jordan L., 22, non-binary
Visit type: Virtual video visit with photos
Reason for visit: Itchy, dry, red patches in the elbow creases and on the forearms for 1 week. History of eczema since childhood.

Assessment: Eczema flare (atopic dermatitis), arms only. No signs of infection.

Plan:
- Betamethasone valerate 0.1% cream: apply a thin layer to the affected areas on the arms twice daily for up to 14 days, then stop.
- Do not use this cream on the face, groin, or armpits.
- Apply a fragrance-free moisturizer at least twice daily, including after bathing.
- Use lukewarm showers and fragrance-free soap.

When to seek care:
- Oozing, yellow crusting, pus, rapidly spreading redness, or fever: book a visit the same day, as this may be an infection.
- No improvement after 14 days: book a follow-up visit.

SYNTHETIC VISIT SUMMARY. Fictional patient, for interview use only. Not medical advice.

Patient: Daniel K., 34, male
Visit type: Virtual video visit with positive rapid strep test from a local pharmacy
Reason for visit: Sore throat and fever for 2 days. No cough.

Assessment: Strep throat (streptococcal pharyngitis).

Plan:
- Amoxicillin 500 mg by mouth twice daily for 10 days.
- Finish the full 10-day course even if you feel better sooner.
- You are considered contagious until you have taken the antibiotic for 24 hours and have no fever. You may return to work after that.
- Ibuprofen (Advil) or acetaminophen (Tylenol) may be used for throat pain or fever as directed on the package.
- Replace your toothbrush after 24 hours on the antibiotic.

When to seek care:
- Trouble breathing, unable to swallow your own saliva, drooling, or a muffled voice: call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department.
- A new rash, or no improvement after 3 days of antibiotics: book a follow-up visit.

SYNTHETIC VISIT SUMMARY. Fictional patient, for interview use only. Not medical advice.

Patient: Priya S., 28, female
Visit type: Virtual video visit
Reason for visit: Burning with urination and urinary frequency for 2 days. No fever, no back or flank pain, not pregnant.

Assessment: Uncomplicated bladder infection (cystitis).

Plan:
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg by mouth twice daily for 5 days (10 doses total). Take with food.
- Finish all 10 doses even if symptoms improve.
- Nitrofurantoin can turn urine dark yellow or brown. This is a harmless side effect.
- Drink plenty of fluids.
- Acetaminophen (Tylenol) may be taken for discomfort as directed on the package.

When to seek care:
- Fever, pain in the back or side, nausea or vomiting: seek in-person care the same day.
- Symptoms not improving after 48 hours of antibiotics: book a follow-up visit.
